citation: Nugent, G., Kunz, G., Houston, J., Kalutskaya, I., Wu, C., Pedersen, J., Lee, S., DeChenne, S. E., Luo, L., & Berry, B. (2016). The Effectiveness of Technology-Delivered Science Instructional Coaching in Middle and High School (Working Paper). Lincoln, NE: National Center for Research on Rural Education (R2Ed), University of Nebraska-Lincoln. Funded by U.S. Department of Education, Institute of Education Sciences (R305C090022). ERIC No. ED571809.
report_number: R2Ed Working Paper (National Center for Research on Rural Education); IES Grant R305C090022; ERIC ED571809
design: School-level (cluster) group-randomized RCT, two cohorts. 124 science teachers (63 treatment, 61 control) in 110 rural schools (61 treatment, 49 control) in Nebraska and Iowa; ~1,000 students of these teachers, split ~equally middle school (48%) and high school (52%). Schools were the unit of randomization. Treatment = 'Coaching Science Inquiry (CSI)' TPD: an 8-day summer institute (over two weeks) teaching a guided scientific-inquiry approach to NGSS science practices, plus 8-12 technology-delivered (WebEx/Dropbox) asynchronous instructional coaching sessions across 6-8 weeks during the school year. Control = business-as-usual (no summer institute, no coaching). Subject = science; grades middle + high school (registry grade band 7-12). Analyzed with 4-level mixed linear models (time within student, student within teacher, teacher within school; REML, Kenward-Roger), cohort as covariate. Student achievement outcomes: science Knowledge (multiple-choice, separate MS and HS forms) and science Practice skills (Student Inquiry Rubric, teacher-rated; only a single post-unit timepoint). Self-efficacy and on-task engagement are non-achievement student outcomes and were not extracted.
problems: This is an 8-page-image but 39-page-text ERIC working paper; the student results live in Tables 5-6 (pp. 23) and narrative (pp. 23-24, 27). Several issues reduce confidence: (1) The report gives Cohen's d for student outcomes only in the narrative (MS Knowledge d=.18; MS Practice d=.34; HS Practice d=.40); HS Knowledge was non-significant (Group x Time Est=0, p=.97) so no d is printed and I record g=0. (2) These d values are NOT explicitly cluster-adjusted: they are standardized mean differences whose magnitude I confirmed reproduces the Table 5 raw post-unit descriptives almost exactly (MS Knowledge raw post d=.17 vs .18; MS Practice .34 vs .34; HS Practice .39 vs .40). The mixed model's school-level random variance is reported in Table 6 but no design-effect ICC is given, so cluster_adjusted=false and icc=null (NOT guessed); n_clusters recorded so it can be Hedges-2007 corrected centrally. (3) Variance uses the sample-size formula on the post-unit n_t/n_c because the reported model SEs in Table 6 are on the raw (unstandardized) coefficient scale and cannot be directly converted to g_se without the standardizing SD; I therefore did not use them. (4) The science Knowledge test is assembled from public independent item banks (SCASS, NAEP, TIMSS) -> labeled standardized_independent though researcher-assembled; the Practice measure (Student Inquiry Rubric) is researcher-made AND rated by the students' own (non-blinded, treatment-assigned) teachers, a notable bias risk. (5) Timepoint: I extract the immediate post-intervention (post-unit) measurement; an end-of-year wave exists only for self-efficacy. (6) The meta-analysis (Visscher et al. 2025) coded this as one effect size; which of these 4 contrasts it used is unknown, so all 4 qualifying STEM achievement contrasts are extracted.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Summer institute + technology-delivered coaching (CSI) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Student science Knowledge multiple-choice test (middle-school form; items drawn from SCASS, NAEP, TIMSS public inquiry-question banks)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post-unit (after teacher delivered the 6-8 week science practice unit)
effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g = J*d using the report's stated Cohen's d=.18 (text p.23, significant). df = n_t+n_c-2 = 820, J = 0.9991, g = 0.9991*0.18 = 0.1798. Confirmed against Table 5 post-unit descriptives: pooled SD = 0.175, raw post d = (0.73-0.70)/0.175 = 0.172 ~= reported .18. Var(d) = (n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c) + d^2/(2*(n_t+n_c)) = 0.004883; Var(g)=J^2*Var(d)=0.004879; g_se=0.0698. impact_estimate/impact_se are the model Group x Time (Time 2) coefficient on the proportion-correct scale (Table 6, MS Knowledge: Est=.02, SE=.01, df=657, p<.05), recorded for traceability but not used to standardize g.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 5 & Table 6 (p. 23); narrative p. 23 ('middle school results were significant... small effect size (d = .18)')
effect_sizes.notes: Significant favorable middle-school science knowledge effect. Model is a 4-level mixed model controlling baseline and cohort; reported d derived from the model. Cluster RCT (schools randomized) but d not cluster-adjusted -> cluster_adjusted=false, n_clusters=110 (icc not reported, not guessed). Achievement (knowledge test), full sample of MS students.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Summer institute + technology-delivered coaching (CSI) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Student science Knowledge multiple-choice test (high-school form; items drawn from SCASS, NAEP, TIMSS public inquiry-question banks)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post-unit (after teacher delivered the 6-8 week science practice unit)
effect_sizes.g_method: Non-significant outcome; no Cohen's d printed. The mixed-model Group x Time (Time 2) coefficient is Est=0.00, SE=.01, p=.97 (Table 6, HS Knowledge), indicating no differential growth -> g=0. (Raw post-unit posttest difference would give d=(0.64-0.62)/0.210=0.095, but both arms gained ~0.03 from baseline so the pretest-adjusted/growth impact is ~0; the model value of 0 is used.) Var(d) sample-size formula at d=0 = (n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c) = 0.004914; Var(g)=J^2*Var(d)=0.004909 (J=0.9991, df=813); g_se=0.0701.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 5 & Table 6 (p. 23); narrative p. 23 ('high school knowledge outcome... showed no significant treatment-control difference')
effect_sizes.notes: Null high-school science knowledge contrast (explicitly the one non-significant student knowledge result). g=0 from the model growth coefficient (Group x Time Est=0, p=.97). Achievement (knowledge test), full sample of HS students.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Summer institute + technology-delivered coaching (CSI) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Student Inquiry Rubric (SIR): teacher-rated student science practice skills (question, investigate, analyze/collect data, explain, communicate; 4-point scale)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post-unit (after teacher delivered the 6-8 week science practice unit)
effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g = J*d using the report's stated Cohen's d=.34 (text p.24; p=.056, 'approached significance'). df = n_t+n_c-2 = 768, J = 0.9990, g = 0.9990*0.34 = 0.3397. Confirmed against Table 5 post-unit descriptives: pooled SD = 0.760, raw d = (3.01-2.75)/0.760 = 0.342 ~= reported .34. Var(d) = (n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c) + d^2/(2*(n_t+n_c)) = 0.005291; Var(g)=J^2*Var(d)=0.005280; g_se=0.0727. impact_estimate/impact_se = model Group fixed effect on the rubric scale (Table 6, MS Practice: Est=.24, SE=.13, df=721, p=.06), recorded for traceability.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 5 & Table 6 (p. 23); narrative p. 24 ('not the middle school... probability level approached significance (.056)... small-medium effect size (d = .34)')
effect_sizes.notes: Middle-school student science-PRACTICE skills, the report's 'key student outcome'. Favorable, p=.056 (FDR/cohort-adjusted), d=.34. CAVEAT: SIR is rated by the students' OWN teachers, who were not blind to condition and were the intervention recipients -> potential rater bias inflating the practice effect; also researcher-made and single-timepoint (no baseline, so not pretest-adjusted). cluster_adjusted=false, n_clusters=110.

effect_sizes.test_name: Student Inquiry Rubric (SIR): teacher-rated student science practice skills (question, investigate, analyze/collect data, explain, communicate; 4-point scale)

effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g = J*d using the report's stated Cohen's d=.40 (text p.24, significant). df = n_t+n_c-2 = 824, J = 0.9991, g = 0.9991*0.40 = 0.3996. Confirmed against Table 5 post-unit descriptives: pooled SD = 0.772, raw d = (3.06-2.76)/0.772 = 0.389 ~= reported .40. Var(d) = (n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c) + d^2/(2*(n_t+n_c)) = 0.004937; Var(g)=J^2*Var(d)=0.004933; g_se=0.0702. impact_estimate/impact_se = model Group fixed effect on the rubric scale (Table 6, HS Practice: Est=.3, SE=.11, df=768, p<.01), recorded for traceability.

effect_sizes.notes: High-school student science-PRACTICE skills, significant favorable effect, d=.40, the report's 'key student outcome'.
